jobs.description:
At Medtronic you can begin a life-long career of exploration and innovation, while helping champion healthcare access and equity for all. You’ll lead with purpose, breaking down barriers to innovation in a more connected, compassionate world.

A Day in the Life
Ihre Chance bei Medtronic – Innovation in der Medizintechnik

Gestalten Sie die Zukunft der Medizintechnik mit Medtronic. Für unser hochinnovatives Produkt Affera suchen wir einen Technical Service Specialist (m/w/d), der modernste Technologien in den klinischen Alltag bringt und damit aktiv zur Verbesserung der Patientenversorgung beiträgt.

Diese Position ist in der Region der Schweiz (Zentralschweiz) zu besetzen. Sie werden hauptsächlich in dieser Region tätig sein und eng mit unseren Kunden vor Ort zusammenarbeiten. Gleichzeitig bietet die Rolle die Möglichkeit, nationale Reisen zu unternehmen, um unsere Kunden in der ganzen Schweiz zu unterstützen. Gelegentlich können auch internationale Reisen erforderlich sein, um an Fortbildungen und Trainings teilzunehmen, die Ihnen helfen, Ihre Fähigkeiten weiterzuentwickeln und auf dem neuesten Stand der Technik zu bleiben.

• Installation, Wartung und Reparatur von Affera‑Systemen bei Kund:innen

• Unterstützung bei der Einführung neuer Geräte und Technologien

• Enge Zusammenarbeit mit Technical Support und internen Schnittstellen

• Sicherstellung von Qualitäts‑, Sicherheits‑ und Compliance‑Standards

• Aufbau vertrauensvoller Kundenbeziehungen durch professionellen Service

• Erfahrung im technischen Service von Medizintechnikprodukten

• Analytische, lösungsorientierte Arbeitsweise

• Hohe Kundenorientierung und Kommunikationsstärke

• Sehr gute Deutsch‑ und gute Englischkenntnisse

• Reisebereitschaft; IT‑/Netzwerkkenntnisse von Vorteil

• Freude an intensivem Austausch mit diversen Personengruppen, ausgeprägte Kunden- und Serviceorientierung sowie starke Kommunikationsfähigkeit und Empathie

• Unternehmerische Denkweise und Ergebnisorientierung

jobs.title: Manufacturing Supervisor (night shift)
jobs.description:
At Medtronic you can begin a life-long career of exploration and innovation, while helping champion healthcare access and equity for all. You’ll lead with purpose, breaking down barriers to innovation in a more connected, compassionate world.

A Day in the Life
Medtronic, a leading global company in the MedTech domain, is hiring a Manufacturing Supervisor responsible for running and transforming the business within the Swiss Manufacturing Operational site (SMO). In the role, you will lead manufacturing operations, provide strategic recommendations on staffing and business needs, eventually committing to value stream accountability, change leadership, team development, as well as coaching and training.

Moreover, you will cultivate an engaging and inclusive work environment, while also utilizing HR processes to address and manage ethical concerns, unplanned absenteeism, and employee performance matters, ensuring alignment with organizational values and policies, eventually overseeing the effective implementation and utilization of Medtronic Performance System (MPS) tools to ensure alignment with established standards to achieve operational consistency and excellence. Responsibilities may include the following and other duties may be assigned:

• Lead manufacturing operations on a night shift to deliver results across safety, quality, delivery, cost, and inventory objectives, by leveraging the disciplined use of Medtronic Performance System, collaborate effectively with cross-functional support teams to drive resolution of abnormalities (5S, EHS risk, quality issues investigation & awareness), including maintenance, quality, engineering, and supply chain, to drive operational excellence and achieve business goals, maintain a strong Gemba presence to gain firsthand insights into operational challenges and provide timely, effective solutions to support shop floor teams

• Communicate clearly and consistently, with a business-mindset, regarding the team's current state, expectations, and priorities, ensuring alignment across teams and execution of optimized production schedules, cultivate an engaging and inclusive work environment that enhances customer value through a motivated, committed and inspired team, with best-in-class standards, exemplifying daily Medtronic Mindset, provide strategic recommendations on staffing and business needs, including manufacturing shift patterns, direct labor recruitment, and prioritization of production activities

• Take ownership of the night shift (people, safety, quality, compliance and delivery) and lead the development and support execution of the shopfloor transformation roadmap to drive operational excellence and deliver measurable business results, design and implement comprehensive development programs for team leaders and operators to develop high-performing teams, eventually cultivating best-in-class routines and establish strong leader standard work to ensure sustainable performance improvements, while also inspiring and engaging teams at all levels to embrace change in a culture of continuous improvement and collaboration, acting as a change agent to promote alignment with organizational goals.

• Ensure alignment & connection with other 2 shifts & day shift support functions.

• Oversee the effective implementation and utilization of Medtronic Performance System (MPS) tools, ensure alignment with established standards to achieve operational consistency and excellence, drive adherence to MPS standards, including tier management, 5S, 5 Whys, A3 problem-solving, and other lean methodologies.

• Drive a culture of standards, leading by example and provide hands-on coaching to team leaders, reinforcing daily adherence to standards and best practices, eventually utilizing HR processes to address and manage ethical concerns, absenteeism, and employee performance matters, ensuring alignment with organizational values and policies.

Required knowledge and experience

• Bachelor’s degree, pref

jobs.description:
We anticipate the application window for this opening will close on - 26 Jun 2026

At Medtronic you can begin a life-long career of exploration and innovation, while helping champion healthcare access and equity for all. You’ll lead with purpose, breaking down barriers to innovation in a more connected, compassionate world.

A Day in the Life
Join our Global Supply Management team as a Category Manager-Electronic Assemblies, where you utilize your strong track record of delivering results in a matrixed organization, where collaboration with diverse individuals, teams, and skill sets is essential for success.

As the Category Manager-Electronic Assemblies, you will partner and lead several categories in electronics, including: PCBA, Power Management, Switch Assemblies, and other electronic assemblies categories. You will use your strong negotiation, technical, and relationship-building skills. As the Category Manager, you will understand global materials markets and possess technical aptitude in secondary processes to develop global strategies that leverage Medtronic’s global purchasing power and deliver cost-effective, innovative solutions to each operating unit within our network. You'll focus on multiple tiers of your supplier’s supply chain to maximize leverage and awareness, ensuring compliance and continuity.

At Medtronic, we bring bold ideas forward with speed and decisiveness to put patients first in everything we do. In-person exchanges are invaluable to our work. We’re working a minimum of 4 days a week onsite as part of our commitment to fostering a culture of professional growth and cross-functional collaboration as we work together to engineer the extraordinary.

As the Category Manager-Electronic Assemblies, you will:

• Lead category strategy development and execution, including best-cost-country sourcing, forward-buy agreements, and supplier innovation in collaboration with engineering and technical sourcing.

• Negotiate and manage supplier contracts that deliver sustained year-over-year improvements in cost, performance, quality, and delivery.

• Build and maintain strong supplier relationships, driving continuous improvement through regular business reviews, performance management, and supplier development initiatives.

• Develop and execute a robust cost-reduction pipeline using lean principles, should-costing, process improvements, tier-2 strategies, yield improvements, and supplier consolidation.

• Analyze markets, quotations, and supplier capabilities to select, recommend, and rationalize suppliers while mitigating supply chain risk and ensuring continuity.

• Leverage data, metrics, and business intelligence to optimize sourcing decisions, improve supplier performance, and independently drive new approaches on complex or strategic initiatives.

• Serve as a strategic advocate for the Supply Management function, partnering with business units and operations to enable and deliver core business objectives. Define and manage winning category strategies and approaches with suppliers.

Must Have: Minimum Requirements

• Bachelor's degree required

• Minimum of 6 years of relevant experience, or an advanced degree with a minimum of 4 years of relevant experience

• Strong knowledge of Electronics & Electronic Assemblies and Suppliers

Nice to Have

• Proven expertise in developing and executing effective negotiation strategies, with strong analytical, problem‑solving, and cross‑functional collaboration skills.

• Solid technical and commercial understanding of commodity markets, manufacturing process technologies, and category‑specific cost and performance drivers.

• Demonstrated experience developing category strategies, building business cases, reviewing contracts, and leading Best‑Cost‑Country sourcing initiatives within a regulated environment.

• Working knowledge of lean manufacturing principles and process improvement methodologies, preferably applied in a manufacturing setting.

• Experience support
